sections.label: Team Singapore Contingent medal haul
sections.summary: The Team Singapore Contingent won two golds, a silver, a bronze, two national records and two personal bests, its best Paralympics medal haul.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Overall, our Team Singapore Contingent had an illustrious campaign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: They came home with two gold medals, a silver and a bronze, two national records and two personal bests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We also brought back our best ever medal haul at the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And amongst our three medallists, two of them, Jeralyn and Max, made it to the podium at the first time of asking, on their debut.

sections.label: Max youngest Olympic sailing medallist
sections.summary: At 17 on his Olympic debut, Max was the youngest Singaporean Olympic medallist and youngest ever to win an individual Olympic sailing medal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At 17 years old and making his debut at the Olympics, Max was not just the youngest Singaporean athlete to win an Olympic medal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: He was also the youngest in the world to win an individual sailing medal at the Olympics ever.

sections.label: Pin Xiu Paralympic gold medals
sections.summary: Pin Xiu won double gold in the S2 Women's 50-metre and 100-metre backstroke, six golds over three Paralympics, her first in 2008.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Pin Xiu is not only Singapore's most decorated Paralympian, having won double gold in the S2 Women's 50-metre and 100-metre backstroke events, over the past three editions of the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: She has effectively made these events her own – six gold medals over three editions of the Paralympics, 50 metres and 100 metres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Remarkedly, Pin Xiu's first gold medal was won 16 years ago in 2008 in Beijing – a champion in every sense.

sections.label: Podiums since 2008 campaigns
sections.summary: Since 2008, over five Olympic and Paralympic campaigns, Singapore has reached the podium at all Paralympics, winning 14 medals in total.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over the past five Olympic and Paralympic campaigns, since 2008, we have been doing incrementally well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have reached the podium at all Paralympics since 2008, winning 14 medals in total.

sections.label: Weekly sports participation growth
sections.summary: Weekly sports participation among Singaporeans grew from 54% in 2015 to 73% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2015, 54% of Singaporeans participated in sports weekly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2023, that figure has grown to 73%.

sections.label: SportCares Bursary participation fees
sections.summary: The SportCares Bursary was set up to cover the full cost of participation fees for those who cannot afford the programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For those who may not be able to afford to be on these programmes, we have set up the SportCares Bursary, which covers the full cost of the participation fees for these programmes.

sections.label: spexScholars numbers growth
sections.summary: The number of spexScholars grew from 61 in 2013 to more than 100 in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The number of spexScholars has grown from 61 in 2013 to more than 100 in the last two years.

sections.label: spexPotential first cohort
sections.summary: This year saw the first cohort of 48 spexPotential athletes, awarded to athletes on the cusp of a breakthrough.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have also gone further upstream, recognising that sometimes we need to give support at an earlier phase in the athlete's development, supporting more promising athletes, earlier on in their sporting journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we saw our first cohort of 48 spexPotential athletes, awarded to athletes who are on the cusp of a breakthrough and who might require that additional nudge or push to help them make the leap.

sections.label: Sports School alumni and scholarships
sections.summary: Over two decades the Sports School produced 19 Olympians and 17 World Champions, and spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships and CPF top-ups were announced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over these two decades, they have produced 19 Olympians and 17 World Champions, some of whom are here today: Amita, Izaac and Shanti are proud alumni of the Sports School.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We also recently announced the spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships and the Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups for our spexScholars.

sections.label: Major Sports Events investment
sections.summary: The Government committed to invest $165 million in Major Sports Events over the next four years, with world-class events and a new 18,000-seater indoor arena.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government has committed to invest $165 million, as the Prime Minister has announced, in the Major Sports Events over the next four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the coming years, Singaporeans can expect world-class events such as the World Chess Championships and the World Aquatics Championships, para swimming, and we will also be building a new 18,000-seater indoor arena, allowing us to host these world-class sports events and also strengthening Singapore’s position as an attractive destination for sports, entertainment and lifestyle.

sections.label: Inclusive swimming pools and gyms
sections.summary: SportSG retrofitted eight swimming pools with wheelchair ramps, two more by end of next year, and targets all ActiveSG gyms inclusive by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SportSG has already retrofitted eight swimming pools with ramps for wheelchairs, two more pools will have ramps by the end of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We also target to make all ActiveSG gyms inclusive by 2026.

sections.label: DSMP disability sport participation
sections.summary: Since the DSMP launch in 2016, sport participation among persons with disabilities rose from 28% in 2015 to 46% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the DSMP in 2016, sport participation among persons with disabilities have increased from 28% in 2015, to 46% in 2023.

sections.label: Singapore Olympic and Paralympic athletes
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore's Olympic and Paralympic athletes inspire and unite Singaporeans, naming Max Maeder, Yip Pin Xiu and Jeralyn Tan as medallists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: More importantly, your efforts and achievements inspire and unite Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: You inspire us all to be faster, higher, stronger; to be the best, or if not, then at least the better versions of ourselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And to do it collectively, together, as one Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Amongst the 23 Olympics and 10 Paralympics athletes who competed, world champion kitefoiler, Max Maeder, six-time Paralympic gold medallist, Yip Pin Xiu, and boccia world number two, Jeralyn Tan, flew our Singapore flag high as they emerged on the podium to receive their hard-fought Olympic and Paralympic medals.

sections.label: Singapore Sports School athletes
sections.summary: The passage states the school produced 19 Olympians and 17 world champions, but none of Singapore's six Olympic medallists is an alumnus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the years, the school has produced 19 Olympians and 17 world champions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some of our athletes have done well to compete at the highest level while balancing their education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, none of our six Olympic medallists till date, Tan Howe Liang, Feng Tianwei, Li Jiawei, Wang Yuegu, Joseph Schooling and Max Maeder, is an alumnus of Singapore Sports School.

sections.label: Athletics coach Luis Cunha
sections.summary: The passage states that athletics head coach Luis Cunha helped Shanti Pereira make her breakthrough after a seven-year plateau.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One example would be athletics head coach, Luis Cunha.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: He helped our “sprint queen”, Shanti Pereira, make her breakthrough after a seven-year plateau.

sections.label: Modified NS programme for Olympians
sections.summary: The passage proposes a modified NS programme for athletes who have competed in the Olympics, noting MINDEF granted deferment to three Olympians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My second suggestion is to implement a modified NS programme for a handful of athletes who have already competed in the Olympics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This suggestion requires a paradigm shift as to the way we view NS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So far, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) has granted deferment only to three Olympians, Joseph Schooling, Quah Zheng Wen and most recently, Max Maeder.

sections.label: Modified NS programme contents
sections.summary: The passage states a modified NS programme could include Basic Military Training followed by a short specialist course, more intensive for a shorter period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A modified NS programme could include Basic Military Training, followed by a short specialist course, something that could be more intensive for a shorter period.

sections.label: Posting retired athletes to SAF
sections.summary: The passage states a retired athlete may be posted back to the SAF as a specialist or coach, and hopes MCCY and MINDEF consider the programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If retired, he may be posted back to the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), to be deployed to the NS reservist units as a specialist, to complete his remaining NS tenure or even serve his time as a coach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I hope MCCY and MINDEF will consider this modified NS programme for Olympians.

sections.label: Parliamentary question on medal rewards
sections.summary: The speaker had filed a Parliamentary Question asking MCCY about cash incentive parameters for SNOC's MGA and its distinction from SNPC's AAA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As those in this House are aware, we currently have programmes that offer monetary rewards for medals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I had previously filed a Parliamentary Question to this House, asking the Minister for MCCY what the parameters were for determining the cash incentive rewards offered under the Major Games Award, or MGA, of the SNOC, and why a distinction existed between the SNOC's MGA and the Athletes' Achievement Awards, or AAA, of the SNPC when measured at comparable international levels.

sections.label: Minister's reply on award bodies
sections.summary: Then-Minister Grace Fu explained that SNOC and SNPC are NGOs, and the MGA and AAA are decided by sponsors and donors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the Parliamentary reply by then-Minister for MCCY Grace Fu, she explained that the SNOC and SNPC were non-governmental organisations (NGOs), and that the MGA and AAA were decided by sponsors and donors.

sections.label: MGA primary sponsor named
sections.summary: The SNOC website states the MGA's primary sponsor is the Tote Board family, comprising Singapore Pools and the Singapore Turf Club.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The SNOC states on its website that the primary sponsor of the MGA is the Tote Board family, comprising Singapore Pools and the Singapore Turf Club.

sections.label: Questioning government influence over awards
sections.summary: The speaker says subsidiaries contribute to nation-building and taxes, so it is difficult to see why the Government cannot exercise greater influence over award amounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Each year, the subsidiaries contribute hundreds of millions to nation-building efforts, and indirectly, to the budget through taxes on betting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, while it is true that the SNOC and SNPC are NGOs, and that the sponsors of the MGA and AAA are varied, it is difficult to see why the Government has decided that it cannot exercise greater influence over the amounts granted by these two sporting award programs.

sections.label: Rewards varying by sport popularity
sections.summary: The speaker says rewarding athletes by eyeballs would mean awards varying by sport, such as soccer, sepak takraw and silat, according to popularity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we were to reward our athletes according to eyeballs, then surely our awards must vary by sport: differing rewards for soccer versus sepak takraw versus silat, in accordance with their popularity.

sections.label: Scoping awards by participation level
sections.summary: The speaker says if participation rules allow global, continental or regional levels, award sizes are scoped accordingly, regardless of eventual sign-ups.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If the rules for participation allow for global, continental or regional, we scope out award sizes accordingly, regardless of how many competitors eventually sign up.

sections.label: Equalising Olympian and Paralympian awards
sections.summary: The speaker argues for equalising monetary awards for Olympians and Paralympians, citing Ms Yip Pin Xiu's comparatively lower reward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To put it in more concrete terms, we should be able to explain why Ms Yip Pin Xiu, our country's most successful sportsperson, has been rewarded comparatively less than others for achievements of a comparable calibre.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe we should take the economically and ethically justifiable step of equalising the monetary awards offered to our Olympians and Paralympians in their respective award programmes.

sections.label: Other countries equalising medal awards
sections.summary: Canada, the US and France are cited as having equalised or increased rewards for Paralympians and Olympians.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Canada announced, at the start of this year, that medals for Paralympians would be equal to those of their Olympian counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The US has done so since 2018 and even renamed their national governing body into the Olympic and Paralympic Committee.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Host nation France increased funding by two and a half times, so that they would be able to reward their medallists equally.

sections.label: Minister Tong on revising DSMP
sections.summary: Minister Edwin Tong has spoken of plans to revise and refresh the DSMP.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Edwin Tong has spoken of plans to revise and refresh the DSMP.

sections.label: Government support for sport
sections.summary: The Government launched the spex scheme 30 years ago and established the Sports School in 2004, with spex grants in 2007 and spex scholarships in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government has been a critical part of this, from launching the spex scheme 30 years ago to establishing the Sports School in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have seen milestones, like the spex grants in 2007 and spex scholarships in 2013, which have transformed the sporting landscape.

sections.label: New spexPotential scheme
sections.summary: The new spexPotential scheme ensures aspiring athletes receive support earlier, before competing for regional and international honours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new spexPotential scheme ensures that aspiring athletes receive support earlier in their journey, long before they compete for regional and international honours.

sections.label: Home of Team Singapore in Kallang
sections.summary: The establishment of the home of Team Singapore in Kallang was announced by the Prime Minister at this year's National Day Rally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The establishment of the home of Team Singapore in Kallang, announced by the Prime Minister at this year's National Day Rally, is another significant milestone.

sections.label: Athlete support and transition
sections.summary: Holistic support helps athletes excel and transition beyond competition, through schemes, scholarships, CPF top-ups, accessible training facilities and mental well-being support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This holistic support enables athletes to excel in their sporting careers and ensures that they are cared for as they transition into life beyond competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have made significant progress in supporting our athletes through initiatives like the spexPotential Scheme, the spexEducation Scholarship and the CPF top-ups for spexScholars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These programmes ensure that their education and future are secure, even as they pursue excellence in sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Equally important, we need to make training facilities more accessible for our para athletes, giving them the space to rise above unique challenges and perform at their best.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us also recognise the need for a dedicated community that supports athletes' mental well-being as they transition into their post-sports careers.

sections.label: Paralympic medallists recognised
sections.summary: Three medallists are recognised: Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximilian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu, with Ms Tan Singapore's first boccia medallist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Their participation in the Games has inspired an entire nation and showcased the best of the Singapore spirit, courage, discipline and teamwork.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This year, we are proud to recognise three medallists, Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximilian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Ms Jeralyn Tan became only our fourth Paralympic medallist when she clinched Singapore's first medal in boccia this year.

sections.label: Max Maeder kitefoiling bronze
sections.summary: Mr Max Maeder achieved a bronze medal in kitefoiling at 17 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Max Maeder has achieved a bronze medal in kitefoiling at just 17 years of age.

sections.label: Yip Pin Xiu gold medals
sections.summary: Yip Pin Xiu won two gold medals in the women's 50m and 100m S2 backstroke events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Yip Pin Xiu won two gold medals in the women's 50m and 100m S2 backstroke events.

sections.label: Patient capital and 2024 medallists
sections.summary: Jacqueline Novogratz explains patient capital, and the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic medallists are celebrated.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Jacqueline Novogratz, the founder and Chief Executive Officer of Acumen, a global non-profit venture capital fund explains that patient capital: “requires that we have incredible tolerance for risk, a long-time horizon in terms of allowing those entrepreneurs time to experiment, to use the market as the best listening device that we have, and the expectation of below-market returns, but outsized social impact.” We used to view winning medals at the Olympic and Paralympic Games as a moonshot.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year, we join Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximillian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu to celebrate their hard-earned medals from the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games.

sections.label: One Team Singapore Fund support
sections.summary: Corporates can contribute to the One Team Singapore Fund, which the Government matches dollar for dollar with a 250% tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More corporates can lead the way by contributing towards the One Team Singapore Fund that provides financial support to sportspersons as well as increase sports' accessibility to vulnerable populations.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To signal its support, the Government matches dollar for dollar for contributions to the Fund and provides a 250% tax deduction to corporate and individual donors.

sections.label: Extending the Fund
sections.summary: The Government could consider extending the Fund beyond its present end date of FY2027 and for a longer term.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government could also consider extending the Fund beyond its present end date of FY2027 and for a longer term.

sections.label: Valuing Athletes' Contribution
sections.summary: Athletes must know their contribution is valued, and employed and self-employed athletes would feel assured and empowered.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Athletes who have invested a significant part of their lives, and oftentimes, youth, must know that their contribution is valued by our society.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Athletes who hold down jobs would feel more assured, knowing that their employers value the diverse perspectives they bring.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Athletes who are self-employed would feel more empowered knowing that their livelihood is recognised and their aspirations and needs are considered in Government policy development.

sections.label: Patient Capital for Athletes
sections.summary: Athletes must know they can count on us to provide patient capital to invest in them and encourage them.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our athletes must know that they can count on us to provide the patient capital to invest in them, to encourage them on and to give them the confidence to overcome, aspire and excel.

sections.label: More for Olympic Qualifiers
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it would consider doing more for athletes and para athletes who qualify for the Olympics and Paralympics, regardless of medals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, would the Government consider doing more for athletes and para athletes who are able to qualify for the Olympics and Paralympics, regardless of whether any medals are won?

sections.label: Parity in Awards
sections.summary: The second point concerns parity in the awards for Olympians and Paralympians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second point has to do with parity in the awards for our Olympians and Paralympians.

sections.label: Paralympian Awards Lagging
sections.summary: Awards for Paralympians still lag behind those of their Olympic peers, a matter covered in today's Straits Times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, this was something that was covered in today's Straits Times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the fact remains that awards for our Paralympians still lag behind those of their Olympic peers.

sections.label: Tote Board funding Paralympian prizes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Tote Board, a Ministry of Finance Statutory Board, can help the SNOC and SNPC get funding so Paralympians receive cash prizes similar to Olympians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a Statutory Board of the Ministry of Finance, I hope that the Tote Board can assist and support the SNOC and SNPC in acquiring the additional funding to ensure that our Paralympians are given similar or identical cash prizes as our Olympians.

sections.label: IRAS guidelines on athlete status
sections.summary: IRAS guidelines recognise an individual's status may change over time, such as between recreational player, athlete employed by a sports body, or trading individual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The very guidelines issued by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore recognise that the status of an individual may change over time, for example, in one year, an athlete could be a recreational player, in the next year, he or she could be an athlete employed by a sports body or they could be an individual carrying on a trade, or similar, in relation to their sporting ability.

sections.label: Athletes donate awards to NSAs
sections.summary: Winning athletes and para athletes must donate a significant part of their awards back to their NSAs, the SNPC, disability sports bodies, funding future training and development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, winning athletes and para athletes are required to donate a significant part of their awards back to their NSAs or to the SNPC and Singapore Disability Sports Council or the National Disability Sports Associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is done in order to help fund future sports training and development, and so in other words, the award money is actually ploughed back into the sports ecosystem.

sections.label: Low risk of revenue leakage
sections.summary: Taking all of this into consideration, the speaker argues the risk of overall revenue leakage is arguably quite low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With all of this taken into consideration, I would make the argument that the risk of overall revenue leakage is arguably quite low.

sections.label: Jeralyn's first Paralympics boccia medal
sections.summary: In September, Jeralyn made history by claiming Singapore's first Paralympics medal in boccia, in her Paralympic debut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In September, Jeralyn made history by claiming Singapore’s first Paralympics medal in boccia, in her Paralympic debut, no less.

sections.label: Two gold medals from Paris
sections.summary: The passage states that the person brought home not one, but two gold medals from Paris.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: You brought home not one, but two gold medals from Paris.

sections.label: Paralympic medals and resolve
sections.summary: Seven golds and one silver across five Paralympic Games are proof of resolve and willpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To perform at such elite standards, with seven golds and one silver across five Paralympic Games, is undeniable proof of your resolve and sheer willpower.

sections.label: Non-participants not interested in sports
sections.summary: Focus group discussions before the 2016 DSMP review found around 70% of non-participants were not interested in sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to focus group discussions with social agencies and SPED schools conducted in the lead-up to the review of the 2016 DSMP, around 70% of non-participants said they were not interested in sports.

sections.label: Equestrians, SDSC pathways, inclusive facilities
sections.summary: Equestrians Laurentia, Hilary and Gemma started riding as therapy, and SDSC offers pathways for high performance sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our equestrians who are with us today – Laurentia, Hilary and Gemma – all started riding as a form of therapy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If you have the interest and desire to challenge yourself in high performance sports, organisations like SDSC have the pathways to make your dreams possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite a fully-equipped and accessible ActiveSG Sports Centre, there was not a single wheelchair user in sight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is my dream that one day, every sports facility will be bustling with activity, where everyone of every ability is included.

sections.label: Yip Pin Xiu Paralympic gold medals
sections.summary: Yip Pin Xiu won two gold medals, giving her seven Paralympic golds and a silver as Singapore's most decorated Paralympian.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On the Paralympic front, we witnessed the legendary Yip Pin Xiu, our champion swimmer, who made history by clinching two gold medals this time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With these victories, Pin Xiu now holds a staggering total of seven Paralympic gold medals and a silver, cementing her status as Singapore's most decorated Paralympian.

sections.label: Jeralyn Tan and Max Maeder medals
sections.summary: Jeralyn Tan debuted in boccia and won Singapore's first Paralympic medal, while Max Maeder won Olympic bronze.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Congratulations too, to Ms Jeralyn Tan, who made her debut in boccia and for securing Singapore's first ever medal at the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And, of course, Olympic bronze medallist young kitefoiler, the charming Mr Max Maeder, the youngest Singaporean to ever win an Olympic medal.

sections.label: Paralympic medal prize money
sections.summary: Pin Xiu received $1.5 million per gold medal and Jeralyn got $300,000 for her bronze medal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Pin Xiu received $1.5 million per gold medal and Jeralyn got $300,000 for her bronze medal.

sections.label: Privately-funded sports awards parity
sections.summary: Awards are privately funded as Government focuses public funds on upstream investments, with sponsors raising Paralympic gold reward from $200,000 to $500,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These awards are privately-funded as the Government focuses public funds on upstream investments for all athletes and the Government has encouraged private sponsors to support these medallists' rewards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And thanks to sponsors like DBS and Tote Board, AAA was, in recent years, enhanced from $200,000 to $500,000 for a Paralympic gold medal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, on this topic of parity of cash awards for both abled and disabled sports champions, I think parity is important, but I also support the Government's approach to the prudent use of public funds for sports recognition.

sections.label: Calling sponsors to equalise awards
sections.summary: The speaker urges Government, Singapore and private sponsors to support equalising cash awards for para and able-bodied athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to look into these needs and I know that MSF and MCCY are looking into this and to allocate more resources too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, on the topic of equalising or the parity of awards, I do call on the Government and the rest of Singapore to join me also in calling upon and, also Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, to call upon the current and potential private sponsors to please also, support us to equalise these cash awards for both para athletes and also able-bodied athletes, so that more resources, including by the Government, can be also spread out to the other very critical and urgent needs.

sections.label: Post-sports career support for athletes
sections.summary: The speaker says stable post-sports careers should be a priority, citing MINDEF's pre-retirement development plans as a reference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For our medallists and sportsmen, securing stable post-sports career should be a priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, programmes that focus on educational opportunities, career guidance and even entrepreneurship for retired athletes should be bolstered to ensure that they thrive beyond their sporting competition years, beyond the sports arena.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And we can actually take reference from the very robust pre-retirement development plans that MINDEF is conducting for its officers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I studied it and I hear very good things about it and the sports fraternity can take a leaf from MINDEF on this area as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, various areas in post-career support, in calling for all to ensure that parity for cash awards is realised, for more investments in sports science and technology, for ensuring greater school participation and developing on sports talents.

sections.label: Expanding sports for disabled participants
sections.summary: Speaking as a social service volunteer, the speaker encourages expanding sports for people with disabilities and special needs who may join future Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Speaking as a volunteer in the social service sector for many years, I would like to say a bit more in the encouragement of expanding and extending sports for those amongst us with disabilities and special needs, that is, those who will potentially participate in future Paralympics and similar sporting events.

sections.label: Funding sports participation by social service providers
sections.summary: The speaker urges Ministries to consider more funding so social service providers can enhance sports participation, ahead of future Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many of our social service providers, though, focus on support that helps achieve basic levels of independence, including employment options when reaching adulthood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, given the organisational support mechanisms in the hands of these organisations and having these in place, enhancing participation in sports for these organisations could be an added focus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To achieve this may need allocation of more funding and I do urge the appropriate Ministries to consider this as we prepare for the upcoming and future Budgets.

sections.label: More support for Paralympians
sections.summary: The speaker says more can be done for Paralympians compared to Olympians, who often have widely promoted commercial sponsorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Compared to our successful Olympians, where commercial sponsorship is often widely promoted and available, we can do more for our Paralympians.

sections.label: Home of Team Singapore
sections.summary: The new Home of Team Singapore and improvements at the Kallang Alive precinct are crucial for the work ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even as we celebrate their victories today, we must not lose sight of the work that lies ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is why the new Home of Team Singapore and its accompanying improvements at the Kallang Alive precinct is so crucial.

sections.label: 2024 Hong Kong dragon boat results
sections.summary: At the 2024 Hong Kong International Dragon Boat Race, the women's team was first runner-up and the men's team second and third runner-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the recent 2024 Hong Kong International Dragon Boat Race, our women's team was placed first runner-up and the men's team placing second and third runner-up against competitors with full-time athletes from China, Thailand and Myanmar.

sections.label: Sports Hub inter-school competitions
sections.summary: Since taking back the Sports Hub, the Government has offered its facilities to host primary and secondary school inter-school competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since the Government took back the Sports Hub, it has offered its comprehensive facilities to host inter-school competitions at the primary and secondary school level, promoting sporting excellence at the highest level and encouraging a select few to further their potential in the international arena.

sections.label: Support for parents and coaches
sections.summary: Home of Team Singapore could offer parenting workshops, coaching seminars and wellness resources so no one in an athlete's life is unsupported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As parents and coaches form the backbone of an athlete's support system, Home of Team Singapore could offer parenting workshops, coaching seminars and wellness resources so that no one in an athlete's life is left unsupported.

sections.label: Medal-winning athletes honoured
sections.summary: Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximilian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu are celebrated for medal-winning performances in Singaporean sports history.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, we celebrate Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximilian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu, whose medal-winning performances have earned them a place of honour in Singaporean sports history.

sections.label: Kallang Alive Masterplan
sections.summary: The Kallang Alive Masterplan and Singapore Sports School relocation are consistent with this approach, as noted by Prime Minister Wong.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recently announced Kallang Alive Masterplan and associated relocation of the Singapore Sports School is consistent with this approach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As noted by Prime Minister Wong in his maiden National Day Rally speech on 18 August 2024, the Masterplan will, and I quote, "assist to strengthen the sporting culture in Singapore and to support all Singaporeans in realising their sporting dreams." Prime Minister Wong went on to say, and I quote, "You don't need to be an elite athlete to enjoy the facilities at Kallang.

sections.label: Olympic participation rarity statistic
sections.summary: A sports commentator noted that only one in 500,000, or 0.000017% of the world's population, ever make it to the Olympics.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As one sports commentator noted, only one in 500,000, or 0.000017% of the world's population ever make it to Olympics.

sections.label: Pin Xiu Paralympic gold medals
sections.summary: Pin Xiu, 32, has won five Paralympic gold medals over three Games and other international medals despite having Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Pin Xiu is a veritable Singapore sporting legend at the age of 32.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: She has won five Paralympic gold medals over three Games and numerous other medals at other international competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Despite having a hereditary neurological disorder called Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease or CMT disease, Pin Xiu has managed to win again and again over the years.

sections.label: Max bronze medal at 17
sections.summary: At 17, Max could not legally order beer in Singapore when he won his bronze medal, and people describe him as level-headed and mature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: At 17 years of age, Max cannot even legally order a can of beer at the neighbourhood coffee shop in Singapore when he won his bronze medal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But everyone who has met him has described him as being level-headed and mature beyond his years.

sections.label: Jannik Sinner Australian Open win
sections.summary: Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner won the Australian Open, the first Italian to do so and currently the first Italian ranked number one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Jannik Sinner, the Italian tennis player, won the Australian Open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: He was the first Italian to have won an Australian Open and currently the first Italian to be ranked number one in the world.

sections.label: Sinner winning next three sets
sections.summary: After 'Weather the storm!', Jannik Sinner's game changed and he won the next three sets 6-4, 6-4, 6-3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Weather the storm!" That was when Jannik Sinner's game changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: He was a different person and then he went on to win the next three sets, 6-4, 6-4, 6-3.

sections.label: Message to Jamus Lim
sections.summary: The speaker tells Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that despite good intentions, he should not create that storm or division in team Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: My message, Mr Speaker, Sir, to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, is that as much as your intentions may be good, please do not create that storm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am sure Minister Edwin Tong will respond later about the incentives, but I think there is no need to try to create any division amongst any one of us, amongst the strong and resilient team Singapore.

sections.label: Equal rewards for athletes
sections.summary: The speaker says calling for equal rewards between para athletes and athletes may be seen as stirring up a storm, and is happy to do so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Far from it being my intention to — firstly, I do struggle to grasp the logic in linking my call for equal rewards between our athletes with creating a storm, but I would only add that if, indeed, calling for equality between our para athletes and athletes constitutes stirring up a storm, then I am happy to be stirring up the storm.

sections.label: New SPED PE syllabus
sections.summary: MOE introduced a new SPED Physical Education teaching and learning syllabus earlier this month, along with helping children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To this end, along with helping children, MOE has introduced a new SPED Physical Education teaching and learning syllabus earlier this month.

sections.label: Disability sport programmes progress
sections.summary: Over the years, a range of disability sport programmes and initiatives have reached close to 20,000 persons with disabilities to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, over the years, we have made good progress, introducing a range of disability sport programmes and initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These have reached out to close to 20,000 persons with disabilities to date.

sections.label: Parasport Academy participants
sections.summary: The Parasport Academy has been launched and so far has more than 400 participants across 10 sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We also have, as you heard me say in my speech earlier, launched the Parasport Academy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so far, there have been more than 400 participants across 10 sports today.

sections.label: Paralympic gold reward amount
sections.summary: Under the Paralympic programme, the reward is $500,000 for each gold, up to three golds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under the Paralympic programme, it is $500,000 for each gold, but it goes up to three golds.

sections.label: Government long-term sports support
sections.summary: The Government uses a year-on-year long-term master plan like the DSMP, building academies, coaches, physiotherapists, sports science, programmes, bursaries and the spex programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In contrast, what the Government does is we look at a year-on-year, long-term master plan, like the DSMP, as an example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We look at building up the academies, like ActiveSG Academies, the Para Sport Academy, the coaches, the specialist physiotherapists that we employ for para athletes, sports science, the programmes that I spoke about earlier in my speech, the various bursaries that we put together, like in SportCares bursaries, as I spoke about in my opening speech as well, to support the lower-income; and, of course, the spex programme, amongst others.

sections.label: Long-term sports investment commitment
sections.summary: The Government commits assured amounts yearly on a long-term masterplan to invest, spend and ensure efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We decide that we want to invest these amounts, spend them, make a commitment and ensure that we have efficiency for the spend that we make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is an assured amount every year, year-on-year, on a long-term masterplan.

sections.label: Government facilities, private sector incentives
sections.summary: The Government leaves incentives to the private sector and Tote Board while committing to facilities that lift the sports base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It does not directly go towards helping those in development, which is what we want to do with a broader spend, so that we can reach and target a broader base mass appeal and developing a pipeline so that more athletes, para as well as able-bodied athletes, can reach the apex of their sport and reach their aspiration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is the thinking that we have in the Government on why we leave the private sector and Tote Board to deal with the incentives while we make commitments here and now and in the long-term on facilities that overall lift the base of sports entirely.

sections.label: Dual-use facilities for public
sections.summary: The Government will work with facilities and schools to make dual-use facilities available to the public on weekends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we will work with facilities; we will work with schools to ensure that on the weekends at least, dual-use facilities are made available as much as possible to the public and in this way satisfy the demand that is building up.

sections.label: Para sports academy and integration
sections.summary: ActiveSG academies have a Para Sports Academy, and NSAs have para sports take part alongside able-bodied athletes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: If he does, then it comes down to, I think, the Government working in tandem with the Tote Board as well as other private donors to try to realise that aspiration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is why our ActiveSG academies now have the Para Sports Academy as well, and to the extent possible, we have NSAs where the para sports take part in the sport side by side with the able-bodied athletes.

sections.label: Tax exemption for athlete awards
sections.summary: A suggestion is made for MCCY to advocate tax exemption for athlete awards, and the sharing formula is discussed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
sentences.text: Would the Minister be able to comment on my suggestion on whether MCCY can advocate for a tax exemption for the awards that are granted to our athletes and para athletes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I will have to check that with the relevant Ministry which is behind me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: You made the point earlier that we should consider the tax exemption because there are a variety of different sharing proportions for the incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think the sharing incentive proportion is designed to reflect the fact that, precisely as I have said today, we have a village behind every athlete and the support structures are something that we value and the split formula that Ms Chandradas spoke about reflects that value – that everyone plays a part in the success of the athlete.
